english.title: Political parties - registered treasurer convicted of offences

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: POLITICAL PARTIES ELECTIONS AND REFERENDUMS ACT 2000

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being registered as treasurer of a political party, namely **(..SPECIFY PARTY..), was convicted, within the period of five years ending with the date of registration,

(A)_[of an offence under the Political Parties, Elections and Referendums Act 2000, namely **(..SPECIFY THE OFFENCE..)]_
(B)_[of an offence committed in connection with a relevant election or referendum within the meaning of Part VII of the Political Parties, Elections and Referendums Act 2000, namely **(..SPECIFY THE OFFENCE..)]_
english.legislation:
Contrary to section 24(8) of and Schedule 20 to the
Political Parties, Elections and Referendums Act 2000.

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Part VII of the Act concerns rules relating to referendums.
(ii) The definition of "referendum" is contained in Section 101(2) and means "a referendum or other poll held, in pursuance of any provision made by or under an Act of Parliament, on one or more questions specified in or in accordance with any such provision".

other.penalty:
A fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
6 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
